extracted.intended_audience: authors seeking literary representation (fiction, nonfiction, and children's authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for querying and proposing books to Folio Literary Management — what genres they accept, submission types (fiction queries vs. nonfiction proposals), and practical advice (query letter and proposal guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio is seeking fiction and nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also has a children's authors and artists division called Folio Jr. Do not target this agency with genres outside their stated needs; check agent pages for any additional specialty notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit "poetry, stage plays, or screenplays."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These genres are expressly excluded from Folio's submissions; submitting them is an anti-pattern and will likely result in automatic rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow agents' specific guidelines for fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: For fiction you need to follow the agents specific guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Folio has multiple agents — consult each agent's individual submission instructions (format, sample pages, synopsis, etc.) and comply exactly. The site emphasizes separate guidelines for fiction queries versus nonfiction proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction proposal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio has separate guidelines for submitting nonfiction proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Folio's provided steps and tips when creating a nonfiction book proposal (structure, components, and presentation). Prepare a full proposal following their guidance rather than sending a fiction-style query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letter expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio provides some great advice for writing a query letter that includes a sample query letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should model their query on the sample and advice provided — craft a concise, professional query that follows Folio's recommended elements and tone. Review agent interviews (e.g., Annie Hwang and Jeff Kleinman) for additional insight into what agents want to see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation scope and suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio Literary Management has over 20 agents and represents established and first-time authors in selling fiction and nonfiction to major publishers throughout the U.S. and around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates the types of authors the agency works with (both debut and established) and the commercial focus (traditional publishing). Use this to assess fit before querying — children's authors may be directed to Folio Jr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find full guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listing points authors to the agency's own submission pages for complete, authoritative instructions. Always follow the agency's live guidelines rather than third-party summaries.
